reason: The fresh baseline varies widely (998–1546 GFLOP/s), so it does not support attributing likely gains from historical noisy comparisons. I ranked the paired-load proposals first: incumbent assembly shows four separate loads, and the supplied probe confirms two paired loads compile correctly, though neither establishes a GEMM gain. The output-transfer proposals have isolated scope and probe support, but the reported speed result came from another implementation. B-panel packing is a worthwhile test: incumbent B loads are strided across reduction steps, but packing adds work and a 64 KiB panel. Panel packing both operands ranks last because it adds more packing and cache pressure. The repeated paired-load proposals describe substantially the same change, so their relative order is not evidence that one variant is better.
